playbook.intent: The top of the backlog is a stack of one-line wishes, the next sprint starts shortly, and the PM and the tech lead are each holding half of what it would take to judge them. The hour is over when the five items on the agenda each carry a ready, needs-info or drop verdict, the ready ones have acceptance criteria and a complexity tag, and everyone who was not in the room can read what changed.
playbook.scope: 1-hour weekly session: PM brings business priorities, tech lead brings tech-debt + capacity reality. Output: top-of-backlog is spec-ready (acceptance criteria + estimated complexity), nothing else. AI agent splits oversized items into sub-tasks.

success-criteria.criterion: Both parties turn up with the pre-read behind them: candidate items carrying outcomes and value notes from one side, feasibility risks flagged from the other, and an agreed list of five to walk
Each of those five leaves the room labelled ready, needs-info or dropped, with none deferred by silence
Items marked ready carry acceptance criteria and a complexity of S, M or L, and no time estimate appears anywhere against them
The backlog itself reflects the calls made, the summary is posted to the team channel, and each needs-info item already has its follow-up on a calendar

stage.name: Pre-Read
stage.intent: PM + tech lead both prep before meeting.

tasks.task: PM brings the candidate items with outcomes + value notes
Tech lead reads the candidates and flags feasibility risks
Both pre-agree the top 5 items to discuss

stage.decision-gate: Advance only when both arrive with the pre-read done.

stage.name: Groom Live

tasks.task: Walk top 5; either ready / needs-info / drop
Write acceptance criteria for ready items

stage.decision-gate: Advance when every top-5 item has a ready/needs/drop verdict.

stage.name: Update & Communicate

tasks.task: Update the backlog with the changes from the meeting
Post the grooming summary to the team channel

stage.decision-gate: Required output: a published grooming summary.
